# Supplementary Appendix {#sec-appendix}

## Appendix A: Mathematical Formulations and Derivations {#sec-app-math}

### Competing-Risk Continuous-Time Hazard Transition Derivation

In our discrete-time Markov simulation model, each annual step $\Delta t = 1.0\text{ year}$ represents the discrete observation of underlying continuous-time transition processes. To guarantee exact demographic conservation and eliminate probability leakage, we derive transition probabilities from the continuous-time transition rate matrix (generator matrix $\mathbf{Q}$).

For cell $i$, let $\lambda_{\text{emig}, i}$, $\lambda_{\text{retire}, i}$, $\lambda_{\text{trans}, i}$, $\lambda_{\text{geo}, i}$, and $\lambda_{\text{age}, i}$ denote the mutually exclusive event hazards, with total exit hazard $\Lambda_i = \sum_{k} \lambda_{k, i}$. Under the assumption of constant hazard rates over the interval $[t, t + \Delta t)$, the survival probability (probability of remaining in cell $i$) is:

$$p_{\text{stay}, i} = \exp\left( -\int_{0}^{\Delta t} \Lambda_i \, du \right) = \exp(-\Lambda_i \Delta t)$$ {#eq-app-stay}

The probability that an individual in cell $i$ experiences event $k$ during interval $\Delta t$ before any competing event occurs is given by the integral of the event-specific hazard multiplied by the survival function:

$$p_{k, i} = \int_{0}^{\Delta t} \lambda_{k, i} \exp(-\Lambda_i u) \, du = \frac{\lambda_{k, i}}{\Lambda_i} \left[ 1 - \exp(-\Lambda_i \Delta t) \right]$$ {#eq-app-event}

Summing across all competing destinations and the stay state yields:

$$\sum_{k} p_{k, i} + p_{\text{stay}, i} = \sum_{k} \frac{\lambda_{k, i}}{\Lambda_i} (1 - e^{-\Lambda_i}) + e^{-\Lambda_i} = \frac{\sum_k \lambda_{k, i}}{\Lambda_i} (1 - e^{-\Lambda_i}) + e^{-\Lambda_i} = (1 - e^{-\Lambda_i}) + e^{-\Lambda_i} \equiv 1.00000000$$ {#eq-app-proof}

This formulation guarantees non-negativity and exact mass conservation for all possible non-negative hazard values.

### Non-Collapsibility of the Odds Ratio (Zhang & Yu Transformation)

Let $p_0$ denote the baseline probability of an event in the unexposed/reference group, and let $p_1$ denote the probability in the exposed group. The true Relative Risk is $\text{RR} = p_1 / p_0$, while the Odds Ratio is:

$$\text{OR} = \frac{p_1 / (1 - p_1)}{p_0 / (1 - p_0)}$$ {#eq-app-or-def}

Solving for $p_1$ in terms of $\text{OR}$ and $p_0$:

$$\frac{p_1}{1 - p_1} = \text{OR} \cdot \frac{p_0}{1 - p_0} \implies p_1 = \frac{\text{OR} \cdot p_0}{(1 - p_0) + (\text{OR} \cdot p_0)}$$ {#eq-app-p1-solve}

Dividing both sides by $p_0$ yields the @zhang1998 transformation:

$$\text{RR} = \frac{p_1}{p_0} = \frac{\text{OR}}{(1 - p_0) + (p_0 \cdot \text{OR})}$$ {#eq-app-rr-zhang}

In our study, applying this equation to the survey findings of @benromdhane2022 ($p_0 = 0.686$) and @dhouib2024 ($p_0 = 0.756$) yields:
- Remuneration dissatisfaction: $\text{OR} = 2.14 \implies \text{RR} = \frac{2.14}{(1 - 0.686) + (0.686 \times 2.14)} = \frac{2.14}{0.314 + 1.468} = 1.19$ (vs. 2.14 unadjusted, an overestimation of +80%).
- Infrastructure deficits: $\text{OR} = 2.48 \implies \text{RR} = \frac{2.48}{(1 - 0.686) + (0.686 \times 2.48)} = \frac{2.48}{0.314 + 1.701} = 1.23$ (vs. 2.48 unadjusted, an overestimation of +102%).
- Workplace violence: $\text{OR} = 2.06 \implies \text{RR} = \frac{2.06}{(1 - 0.756) + (0.756 \times 2.06)} = \frac{2.06}{0.244 + 1.557} = 1.14$ (vs. 2.06 unadjusted, an overestimation of +81%).

### Iterative Proportional Fitting (IPF) Algorithm

The 36-cell baseline stock tensor $S_{a,s,r,k}(0)$ was initialized by minimizing discrimination information subject to marginal constraints from INS and Carte Sanitaire 2023:

$$\min \sum_{a,s,r,k} S_{a,s,r,k} \ln\left( \frac{S_{a,s,r,k}}{S_{a,s,r,k}^{(0)}} \right)$$ {#eq-app-ipf}

subject to:
$$\sum_{a,r,k} S_{a,s,r,k} = M_{s}^{\text{INS}}, \quad \sum_{a,s,k} S_{a,s,r,k} = M_{r}^{\text{Carte}}, \quad \sum_{a,s,r} S_{a,s,r,k} = M_{k}^{\text{Carte}}$$

The algorithm iteratively updates cell headcounts along each margin until the maximum cell difference between successive iterations is less than $10^{-6}$.

## Appendix B: Comprehensive Parameter Provenance Registry {#sec-app-parameters}

Every model parameter is classified into the formal 5-tier identification hierarchy (@tbl-app-params):
- **Class A**: Directly estimated from Tunisian empirical data.
- **Class B**: Regional North African / Maghreb benchmarks.
- **Class C**: Pooled international meta-analyses or multi-country panel econometrics.
- **Class D**: Structural demographic identities and health economic standards.
- **Class E**: Standardized policy counterfactual scenario levers.

## Appendix C: CHEERS 2022 Reporting Checklist {#sec-app-cheers}

The study methodology and reporting strictly adhere to the 28-item Consolidated Health Economic Evaluation Reporting Standards (CHEERS 2022) Statement [@husereau2022], summarized in @tbl-app-cheers.

| Item No. | CHEERS Section & Item | Reported in Manuscript | Location & Description |
| :---: | :--- | :---: | :--- |
| **1** | Title | Yes | Title page: Identifies dynamic workforce simulation, policy counterfactuals, and economic evaluation to 2050. |
| **2** | Abstract | Yes | Abstract: Structured summary with objectives, methods, milestone outcomes, and policy implications. |
| **3** | Background and Objectives | Yes | Section 1: Institutional context, brain drain escalation, and explicit primary/secondary objectives. |
| **4** | Health Economic Analysis Plan | Yes | Section 2: CHEERS 2022 and Second Panel compliant plan specified prior to model execution. |
| **5** | Study Population | Yes | Section 2: Entire licensed and practicing physician workforce in Tunisia (36-cell tensor). |
| **6** | Setting and Location | Yes | Section 2: National Tunisian health system, disaggregated into Coastal and Interior macro-regions. |
| **7** | Comparators | Yes | Section 2: Status Quo baseline (SCEN_0) versus 5 standardized policy counterfactuals. |
| **8** | Perspective | Yes | Section 2: Public payer perspective (Ministry of Health and Ministry of Finance). |
| **9** | Time Horizon | Yes | Section 2: 25-year projection horizon (2025–2050) with milestone reporting at 2030, 2040, and 2050. |
| **10** | Discount Rate | Yes | Section 2: Baseline 3.0% annual discount rate; tested at 0.0%, 5.0%, and 8.0%. |
| **11** | Selection of Outcomes | Yes | Section 2: Total, public-sector, and interior-region physician-years retained; emigrants averted. |
| **12** | Measurement of Outcomes | Yes | Section 2: Exact continuous-time competing-risk multi-state Markov transitions. |
| **13** | Valuation of Outcomes | Yes | Section 2: Natural units (physician-years retained); complementary operational support factor (35%). |
| **14** | Measurement and Valuation of Resources | Yes | Section 2: Full inframarginal public wage bill expansion, capital budgets, and net training investment losses. |
| **15** | Currency, Price Date, and Conversion | Yes | Section 2: 2024 Tunisian Dinars (TND); historical series deflated by INS Consumer Price Index. |
| **16** | Model Type and Rationale | Yes | Section 2: Discrete-time 36-cell Markov stock-and-flow model with continuous-time hazard engine. |
| **17** | Assumptions | Yes | Section 2 & Appendix A: Documented baseline filter timing ($\alpha$), realization ($\kappa$), and policy decay. |
| **18** | Analytical Methods | Yes | Section 2: 2-parameter MLE calibration, temporal validation split, and external DREES/BÄK validation. |
| **19** | Study Results: Baseline Stock & Flow | Yes | Section 3: Calibrated 36-cell stock, in-sample and out-of-sample fit metrics (MAPE, RMSE, $r$). |
| **20** | Study Results: Resource Use and Costs | Yes | Section 3 & Table 3: Undiscounted and discounted fiscal costs across all scenarios. |
| **21** | Study Results: Cost-Effectiveness | Yes | Section 3: Cost-Consequence Analysis, ICERs ($\text{ICER}_{\text{public}}, \text{ICER}_{\text{interior}}$), and efficiency frontier. |
| **22** | Study Results: Uncertainty Analysis | Yes | Section 3: Deterministic Tornado analysis and 1,000-draw Monte Carlo PSA credible intervals. |
| **23** | Study Results: Heterogeneity | Yes | Section 3: Disaggregated outcomes by career stage, sector of practice, geography, and specialty. |
| **24** | Discussion: Findings & Policy | Yes | Section 4: "Training-only trap", infrastructure efficiency, synergistic bundling, and fiscal feasibility. |
| **25** | Discussion: Limitations | Yes | Section 4: Aggregated specialty clusters, stationary return migration, and absence of DALYs. |
| **26** | Discussion: Generalizability | Yes | Section 4: Transferability of findings to Maghreb (Morocco, Algeria) and middle-income health systems. |
| **27** | Source of Funding | Yes | Declarations: Independent academic research conducted without external commercial sponsorship. |
| **28** | Conflicts of Interest | Yes | Declarations: Authors declare no competing financial or professional interests. |
